lines.text: A recruiter hands you three resumes and says: shortlist the best two.
You wouldn't answer in one breath. You'd read one, note a score, read the next. Each step depends on the last.
An agent works the same way. It's the tool call from last lesson, inside a loop.
Think: the model reads everything so far and picks a tool. Act: your code runs it. Observe: the result joins the conversation.
Then round again. List the files. Read a resume. Save a score. Every lap, the message list grows.
When the model replies with plain text and no tool call, that's the final answer, and the loop ends.
But a stuck model can repeat the same call forever, and every lap costs tokens. So you set max steps: a hard stop.
Add a token budget as well, so one bad run can't drain your credits.
And when a tool fails, don't crash. Send the error back as an observation, and the model usually corrects itself.
That message list is the agent's only memory. Your code resends all of it on every turn, so keep tool results short.
So an agent is just a model, some tools, and a loop that always knows when to stop.
Next lesson: guardrails, before your agent sends a single email.
